final_answer:
Bread-spikers were defined as subjects whose mean non-mitigated bread-meal peak glucose rise exceeded the cohort median (median = 56.4621 mg/dL). After averaging metabolomics replicates to the subject level, merging with clinical metadata, and fitting linear regressions of systolic blood pressure on each candidate metabolite with age and BMI as covariates, only one hypertension-associated metabolite met the required positive-direction and significance criteria within the bread-spiker group.

Top hits passing criteria within bread-spikers (up to 10 requested):
1. N-Acetylgalactosaminitol — beta = 0.007538, 95% CI 0.003009 to 0.012067, p = 0.004053, BH-FDR q = 0.004053, n = 14 bread-spikers.

No additional metabolites passed the same criteria, so the top-10 list contains only this single qualifying metabolite.

Assumption used because the files did not include a pre-labeled hypertension-metabolite set: “hypertension-associated metabolites” were operationalized as metabolites positively associated with systolic blood pressure in the full merged cohort after adjustment for age and BMI. Under that definition, N-Acetylgalactosaminitol was the only metabolite that also remained significantly positively associated with systolic blood pressure within bread-spikers.
